# Kide

> Pip the Sprout gets sleepy and asks to be tucked in, so screen time ends on Pip's terms instead of yours. Teaches colors, counting and shapes out loud, plus pretend-play potty and handwashing routines that are never scored. A parent account is optional. No ads, and nothing a child says ever leaves the device.

No ads, and nothing a child says leaves the device. Not a substitute for a speech-language pathologist's assessment.

## Start here
- [Kide — The Screen Time That Ends Without a Meltdown](https://kide.us/): Pip the Sprout gets sleepy and asks to be tucked in, so screen time ends on Pip's terms instead of yours. Teaches colors, counting and shapes out loud, plus pretend-play potty and handwashing routines that are never scored. A parent account is optional. No ads, and nothing a child says ever leaves the device.
- [Pip the Sprout — Grow & Learn | Kide](https://kide.us/play): A joyful, adaptive learning game for toddlers. Pip the Sprout reads every question out loud — and can listen for spoken answers — so little ones learn colors, counting, shapes, letters and feelings before they can read. A parent account is optional. No ads, no voice recordings, nothing a child says ever leaves the device.
- [Speech sounds by age: what your child should be saying, and when](https://kide.us/sounds): Tap an age and see which sounds are usually in place and which are still developing. The ages come from the reviews linked on the page. Word lists to practice at home. Free, and nothing is scored.
- [Say it with me — Kide](https://kide.us/words): Your child chooses a companion, names them, and helps them through a world where every word is a little bit of speech practice. Nothing is scored. Nothing ever leaves the device.
- [Kide for speech-language pathologists: home-practice evidence you can put in a chart](https://kide.us/for-slps): A home-practice record with per-phoneme accuracy, adherence, and trend detection — generated on the family's device. Free for families. No audio, no voiceprints, and nothing from the practice record reaches a server.

## Speech sounds, one page per sound
- [The "b" sound: one of the first sounds children make](https://kide.us/sounds/b): When children usually learn the "b" sound, whether a missing one is on time, and words to practice it. The studies are named on the page. Nothing is scored.

- [The "h" sound: the consonant with nothing to place](https://kide.us/sounds/h): When children usually learn the "h" sound, whether a missing one is on time, and words to practice it. The studies are named on the page. Nothing is scored.

- [The "m" sound: the sound you can make with your mouth closed](https://kide.us/sounds/m): When children usually learn the "m" sound, whether a missing one is on time, and words to practice it. The studies are named on the page. Nothing is scored.

- [The "p" sound: the puff of air you can see](https://kide.us/sounds/p): When children usually learn the "p" sound, whether a missing one is on time, and words to practice it. The studies are named on the page. Nothing is scored.
- [The "r" sound: the last sound to arrive, and why](https://kide.us/sounds/r): When children usually learn the "r" sound, whether a missing one is on time, and words to practice it. The studies are named on the page. Nothing is scored.

## Guides for parents
- [Guides — Kide](https://kide.us/guides): Why Pip's routines are built the way they are, in plain language — the research behind no-score potty training, the screen time that ends itself, and keeping your child's voice on the device.
- [Why Pip's potty routine is never scored — Kide Guides](https://kide.us/guides/potty-training-without-pressure): A material reward can make toddlers less helpful once it is withdrawn, and stool-toileting refusal is associated with constipation. Here's the research behind Pip's Turn, and why nothing about going potty is scored, timed, or rewarded.
- [The screen time that ends without a fight — Kide Guides](https://kide.us/guides/screen-time-that-ends-itself): Most screen-time apps end with a limit you enforce. Pip ends by getting sleepy and asking to be tucked in, so your child is part of the ending instead of on the losing end of it.
- [Why we don't send your child's voice anywhere — Kide Guides](https://kide.us/guides/your-childs-voice-stays-on-the-device): If a browser can't understand speech without sending it to a server, Pip doesn't offer the microphone there at all. No cloud fallback exists to switch on by mistake. Here's exactly how that works today.

## More
- [Toddler in a cast? Pip's Cast Club helps little ones heal — Kide](https://kide.us/cast): A gentle recovery companion for a preschooler with a broken leg or arm. Pip gets a cast too, counts the sleeps to the doctor visit, gives stickers for resting and plays sitting-still games. Free to start, no account.
- [Make a card · Kide](https://kide.us/make): Build a card for a child you know. Choose who is on it, what they look like, and what it says — then send the link. The card is not saved on our servers. This page sends a note of the page, a halfway scroll, and each button or link tapped: the words on that control and, for a link, its address. On this page those words can be a card choice or a name on the picture, and the Open link's address contains the names and the note.
